# Roadmap

Part of the [audience_score_system product brief](../PRODUCT.md).

Each `Cn` below is defined in [`02-capability-map.md`](02-capability-map.md).

_`Status` is each milestone's **current** delivery status, derived from krill's append-only `milestone_status_event` history (`store.MilestoneStatusEventStore.CurrentStatuses`). A milestone with no recorded transition is `not started` — that is krill's own derivation from the absence of history, not a rendered default._

7 milestones (0 abandoned), one block each below.

### M1 — A single Creator and Analyst can run one idea through all three loops end-to-end, on one Channel

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C9, C10
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB2, LB3, LB4
- Deliberately deferred: Multi-Channel [C11] (→ M2); Analyst-across-Channels [C12] (→ M2); Multi-Creator-per-Channel [C13] (→ M2); Calibration trends across many ideas [C14] (→ M3); Creator delegation of research guidance [C15] (→ Later, unscheduled); Deeper Analytics metrics [C16] (→ Later, unscheduled)
- FR budget: 24

FR budget 24 is deliberately above the default: this milestone is the founder's stated V1 scope philosophy in full (all three loops connected, shallow rather than deep), so its capabilities span OAuth/signup, invite/accept, research write-back, viability verdicts, schedule sync, schedule draft/approve, and outcome comparison. Splitting it would produce a milestone ending in a component ("the research store", "the schedule API") rather than a persona doing something, and the founder explicitly ruled it out ("do not let M1 shrink to just one loop").

History: as originally scoped M1 also delivered C6, C7 and C8 (synced schedule view, schedule draft, draft approval). Amendment `video-script-model` (issue #1562) retired all three; their numbers are retired in krill and not reused, so they no longer appear in Delivers. C7/C8 were superseded by C18/C19 (M2.1); C6 was cut entirely.

### M2 — A Creator with several Channels, and the Analysts and co-Creators on them, all work across every Channel they're associated with

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C11, C12, C13
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB2, LB3
- Deliberately deferred: Calibration trends across many ideas [C14] (→ M3); Creator delegation of research guidance [C15] (→ Later, unscheduled); Deeper Analytics metrics [C16] (→ Later, unscheduled)
- FR budget: 12

FR budget 12: mostly authorization and list-view plumbing over the join table LB2 already established in M1; no new loop, no new external integration. This is the milestone that exercises the join table's role-scoped authority checks beyond one row per role, and it must not require per-Channel re-consent as connected accounts multiply (LB1).

### M2.1 — A Creator or Analyst can turn a viable idea into a greenlit video script and see how it tracked to the published video, with no schedule/calendar step in between

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C18, C19
- Must not foreclose: LB2, LB3, LB4
- FR budget: 12

M2.1 is not a sub-phase of shipped M2 — the decimal denotes sequence position only, between M2 and M3, following the same independent-milestone precedent M4.x set.

Also delivers (a Requirement; the renderer's Delivers line lists capabilities only): C19 — "Web surface: review, approve, deny and browse video scripts". The web review/approve/deny and video-script browse slice shipped with this milestone in issue #1834.

Deliberately deferred: none — this milestone re-cuts Loop 2 rather than extending it; pacing/calendar mechanics are removed, not deferred (amendment `video-script-model`, issue #1562).

FR budget 12 covers: new `video_script` store methods and authz checks (C18/C19), retiring the pacing/schedule-draft/commit store surface, C9/C10's FK retarget from schedule drafts to video scripts, and re-anchoring the already-shipped M1 outcome-matching path (`list_pending_matches`/`resolve_pending_match` and the `get_prediction_vs_outcome` read) from `schedule_entry` to `video_script`. That re-anchor was not a mechanical FK swap: `worker/sync/matching.go` scored auto-link candidates as `titleWeight(0.7)*titleSimilarity + dateWeight(0.3)*dateProximity` against `MatchConfidenceThreshold = 0.8`, and removing the scheduled-date signal caps title-only scoring at 0.7 — below the auto-link threshold by construction. Resolving that (a target-date field on `video_script`, retuned weights/threshold, or accepting auto-link's effective removal) was real matching-logic design work inside this milestone, which is why the budget sits at the upper end of the milestone-sized range.

### M3 — A Creator or Analyst can see how well the system's predictions have tracked reality across every idea on a Channel, not just one at a time

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C14
- Must not foreclose: LB2, LB3
- Deliberately deferred: Creator delegation of research guidance [C15] (→ Later, unscheduled); Deeper Analytics metrics [C16] (→ Later, unscheduled)
- FR budget: 8

FR budget 8: a read-side aggregate view over data every prior milestone already produces, plus one narrow new write path — a per-Channel outcome-bar setting (metric_name/threshold_value, views-only for M3; CanWrite for Creator or Analyst; same shape as the retired pacing_policy; see #1880's FR1). Trend queries must stay correctly scoped per person's Channel associations (LB2), and this milestone is the aggregate query LB3's FK chain exists to make cheap.

Later-bucket capabilities (C15, C16) are deliberately left unscheduled past M3: the founder's V1 scope philosophy is that V2 iterates on whichever loop proves weakest, which isn't knowable until M1-M3 are in dogfood use.

### M4.1 — A Creator or Analyst can save and browse Loop 1 (research notes + viability verdicts) entirely from the web UI

- Status: shipped
- Must not foreclose: LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5
- Deliberately deferred: Loop 2 UI parity (web surface for video scripts) (→ M4.2); Loop 3 UI parity (web surface for C9, C14, and C10's prediction-vs-outcome browsing slice) (→ M4.3)
- FR budget: 12

Delivers (Requirements; the renderer's Delivers line lists capabilities only, so none appears above):
- C4 — "Web surface: save and browse research notes"
- C5 — "Web surface: save and browse viability verdicts"
- C10 — "Web surface: browse research notes and verdicts"

The MCP surfaces shipped in M1. A web-side research/viability *reasoning* surface is not deferred — it stays MCP-agent-only (or an embedded whagent-net session, C21) permanently, per the no-own-agent-loop non-goal.

FR budget 12: a `web` front end (save forms + read views) over `store.ResearchStore`/`store.VerdictStore` and the `store.CanX` checks M1's MCP tools established; no new integration, no new schema, comparable in shape to M2's join-table plumbing. This milestone establishes LB5's shared-store-and-authz pattern for the first time and appends its own NFR3 amendment paragraph to `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

### M4.2 — A Creator or Analyst can propose a video script from the web UI, completing web parity for Loop 2 (review, approve, deny and browse had already shipped with M2.1)

- Status: shipped
- Must not foreclose: LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5
- Deliberately deferred: Loop 3 UI parity (web surface for C9, C14, and C10's prediction-vs-outcome browsing slice) (→ M4.3)
- FR budget: 12

Delivers (a Requirement; the renderer's Delivers line lists capabilities only, so none appears above): C18 — "Web surface: propose a video script from the Idea page" (`POST .../ideas/{id}/video-scripts`; PR #1918).

Re-specced after M2.1. The milestone was originally defined as web UI over the schedule/pacing store methods (C6/C7) plus a schedule-drafts browsing slice of C10. Once M2.1's `video_script` model retired those, plan #1914 re-derived its scope: review/approve/deny (C19) and the video-script browse slice of C10 had already shipped in #1834 with M2.1 and are credited there, so the one gap this milestone closed is propose-from-web (C18), which until then existed only as the `save_video_script` MCP tool. Also shipped: the milestone's NFR3 amendment (#1919) and an e2e test (#1921).

FR budget 12 is the original definition's value, kept as defined; most of the original scope was retired or had already shipped, so the milestone ran well under it.

Reuses the shared store+authz pattern M4.1 established (LB5) and appends its own NFR3 amendment paragraph.

### M4.3 — A Creator or Analyst can compare predicted vs. actual outcomes and browse calibration trends across ideas entirely from the web UI

- Status: shipped
- Must not foreclose: LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5
- FR budget: 10

Delivers (Requirements; the renderer's Delivers line lists capabilities only, so none appears above):
- C9 — "Web surface: outcome metrics and pending-match confirm/reject"
- C10 — "Web surface: browse prediction-vs-outcome comparisons"
- C14 — "Web surface: calibration trends and outcome bar"

Deliberately deferred: none further — this closes M4's UI-parity scope. C15/C16's interface allocation stays unspecified/unscheduled, and C17 (Next, scheduled-but-unallocated per the `channel-history-grounding` amendment) is unaffected.

FR budget 10: read-side rendering (outcome comparison, calibration-trend aggregate) plus pending-match confirm/reject, over store methods `mcp`'s C9 tools and M3's C14 aggregate query established; no new write path beyond confirm/reject. Appends its own NFR3 amendment paragraph to `ARCHITECTURE.md`. Depends on M3 (C14) having shipped — the calibration-trend aggregate this milestone renders doesn't exist before M3.

## Later coverage

_Capabilities no milestone delivers, with the load-bearing decisions recorded as protecting them (krill `lb_protects_feature` edges). A capability with none is uncovered._

- C15 — A Creator can delegate close guidance of research steps to an Analyst, reducing the Creator's direct involvement in Loop 1.: uncovered
- C16 — A Creator or Analyst can see deeper Analytics metrics beyond views/retention/CTR (e.g. audience retention curves, traffic sources, subscriber conversion), deepening whichever loop proves weakest.: LB1 — Deeper Analytics (retention curves, traffic sources, subscriber conversion) rides on the scope already held at initial consent.
- C17 — A Creator or Analyst can ground a viability discussion in the Channel's own content history and comparable channels, not just topic research.: uncovered
- C20 — A Creator or Analyst can see a Channel's recent (24h / 7d) activity and outcome trend on the Channel dashboard.: uncovered
- C21 — A Creator or Analyst can run a research agent inside ASS's web UI that acts as them against ASS's MCP tools, embedding a whagent-net session.: LB6 — An embedded session a Creator/Analyst can't watch update live is a black box with a submit button, so live-following is C21's core behavior.
- C22 — A Creator or Analyst can browse a Channel's published videos with title, date and sync-status filters.: uncovered
